div.p: Assured as are peace and guarantees necessary for all men of good will that they devote themselves to the development of industrial enterprises in the territory dominated by the Constitutionalist army, giving employment to the laborers that aid in the development of the industries which constitute the public wealth; it is made known to proprietors or managers of all classes of enterprises that have not undertaken a renewal of work that there is given a period of one month which is not subject to further extension, dating from the date of this decree, in which must be reinstituted work interrupted because of the abnormal situation through which we have passed, and after the conclusion of the period named there will be imposed upon those who have failed to comply with the foregoing requirement as a first step a fine equal to an increase of 50% in the taxes which are ordinarily paid into the treasury, without prejudicing the taking of other steps which may be made necessary if they still persist in the continued close of their respective industries, which while not benefiting the proprietors, does great harm to the villages which have been formed under the shadow of concessions granted by the government and which the concessionaires have not known how to appreciate, such concessionaires now showing themselves timid without any reason which can justify the proceeding which it is designed to correct.
In view of the foregoing and in virtue of the extraordinary powers with which I find myself clothed, I find it proper to decree the following:

There is given one month, counted from this date, for renewing mining, industrial and other operations which have been closed because of the war, and upon the owners or agents who do not renew operations within the period named there will be forthwith imposed an increase of 50% in the taxes ordinarily paid. However, this payment will not be considered as releasing the parties not resuming work of responsibility for hardships that might be resented by the residents of those villages, which, formed under the shadow or the respective enterprises, especially those engaged in the operation of mines, are dependent upon such enterprises.
Ordered printed, published and circulated in order that due observance may be given.
